Sam: Quick sync follow-up on lazy RBAC eval. Can we avoid pushing full policy into the planner and still get secure, low-cost plans?
Rina: Short answer: yes, if we split shape-affecting rules (go to planner) vs auth-only checks (post-filter).
Hector: Main worry: post-filter may waste work (scanning large tiles) and blow up p99. Need a cheap short-circuit.
Zoe: Proposal: planner accepts an "auth_hint" predicate (opaque) with a selectivity estimate from the policy service. Planner uses it for plan selection but doesn't embed full policy logic.
Sam: Example header: X-Auth-Hint: "{\"predicate\":\"tenant_id=42\",\"selectivity\":0.01}" — cheap and explicit.
Rina: How do we keep selectivity honest? Instrument sampled queries and maintain a rolling EWMA per-(route, tenant) in the policy service.
Hector: Add executor metrics: auth.hint_selectivity_observed and auth.hint_drift_ratio. Alert if drift >2x over 5m.
Zoe: Enforcement: deny-critical rules still sync-checked in executor entrance. Non-critical GA gates can be lazy: post-filter before materialization so we avoid returning forbidden rows.
Sam: Edge case: shared tiles. If auth_hint reduces sharing, we need tile_fingerprinting and an opt-in route.tile_sharing flag.
Rina: Perf harness: simulate 50k tenants with mixed selectivity and 5% misestimated hints. Measure p50/p95/p99 and plan_repick_count.
Hector: Mitigation playbook: if plan_repick_count spikes, auto-degrade route -> precomputed aggregates. ops runbook to rollback hinting flag.
ops-bot: CI: auth-hint-proxy integration tests passed (build #2157) :white_check_mark:
Sam: Next actions: short RFC addendum (hint schema, EWMA buckets, metrics, enforcement tiers). I'll draft and ping reviewers.
Rina: I'll own perf scenarios and sampling infra.
Hector: I'll write alert thresholds and degrade automation.
Zoe: I'll prototype the auth-hint header encoder in the policy service.
Sam: Thanks — concise plan. :thumbsup:
